summary: Yardbarker previews the NFL's Christmas Day triple-header: Raiders at Chiefs, Giants at Eagles, and Ravens at 49ers. The article highlights storylines for each game, including the Mahomes-Crosby rivalry, struggling Eagles units, and the 49ers-Ravens game as a possible Super Bowl LVIII preview with MVP implications for Brock Purdy and Lamar Jackson.
one_line: Preview of the NFL's Christmas Day triple-header, led by the 49ers-Ravens clash as a potential Super Bowl LVIII preview and MVP race showdown.
key_facts: The NFL's Christmas Day slate is a triple-header: Raiders (6-8) at Chiefs (9-5) at 1 p.m. ET, Giants (5-9) at Eagles (10-4) at 4:30 p.m. ET, and Ravens (11-3) at 49ers (11-3) at 8:15 p.m. ET.
Kansas City holds a 10-1 record over the Raiders since Patrick Mahomes became its starting quarterback; Maxx Crosby has five sacks in nine career games against the Chiefs.

Raiders rookie fourth-rounder Aidan O'Connell led seven touchdown scoring drives in a 63-21 win over the Chargers, and has thrown for 1,300 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions in six games as the full-time starter.

Travis Kelce averages 89.6 yards per game with Taylor Swift in attendance this season, but had his worst outing in her presence last time, with five catches for 28 yards; he averages 81.3 receiving yards per game against the Raiders since 2019.
The Eagles are on a three-game losing streak and their defense, with Matt Patricia as play-caller, has given up the third-most points in the NFL during it (95).
The Giants have surrendered 76 sacks, the third-most in a single season in NFL history, and their last win at Lincoln Financial Field came in 2013.

Eagles scored only four offensive touchdowns during their skid, three via the 'tush push', after averaging 28.2 points over the first 11 games; the Giants allow 131.6 rushing yards per game, fourth-most in the league.
Giants undrafted rookie Tommy DeVito has thrown for 858 yards, seven touchdowns and one interception in five starts, with a 97.3 passer rating.
The 49ers-Ravens game pits the top seed in each conference and could be a Super Bowl LVIII preview; per oddschecker, Brock Purdy is the MVP favorite at -230 and Lamar Jackson is second at +525.
Purdy, the final pick of the 2022 NFL Draft, is 23 and leads the NFL in QBR (76) and touchdown passes (29), and is third in passing yards (3,795), despite offseason elbow surgery.
Lamar Jackson has 3,105 passing yards, 17 touchdowns, and 741 rushing yards with five scores in his first season under OC Todd Monken.
Christian McCaffrey leads the NFL in rushing (1,292 yards) and total yards per game (128.6) and is tied for first in touchdowns (20).
Ravens tight end Isaiah Likely has averaged 64.3 yards over his last three games, replacing Mark Andrews (ankle injury in Week 11), who averaged 54.4 yards per game before getting hurt.
The Ravens defense allows the fewest points per game (16.1); the 49ers rank second in points allowed (16.7) and lead the NFL with 25 turnovers.
